minutes.headline: Conservation Commission voted to fine a Townsend Street landowner for silt reaching Page Pond.
minutes.summary: The commission heard several wetlands hearings by Zoom. It continued 41 Country Lane and 101 Pleasant Street to December 1 and issued determinations on three smaller projects. It also took up silt runoff from 615 Townsend Street and voted on a written notice of fines for any further silt reaching Page Pond.

attendees.role: member (absent at roll call, joined later)

public_comment.topic: Thanked the commission for its work on the 101 Pleasant Street project. Said the applicant's consultants first contacted her in April and she had advised a smaller project.
Suggested design alternatives for the 41 Country Lane house, such as tucking the garage under or putting auxiliary rooms upstairs, to shorten the footprint while keeping single-floor living.
Asked the 35 Peninsula Drive applicants about side setbacks and endorsed rearranging the layout.
Directed the board and the applicant to her June 14 comment letter on 101 Pleasant Street. It covered wetland crossings, monitoring of replication by a qualified person, and a clerk of the works.
Thanked the commission for acting on 615 Townsend Street. Said the violations have run six years, stockpiles have grown, and the attorney recommended a separate wetland scientist and peer review.

budget_items.what_was_said: The agent asked the commission to ratify spending for pest control and septic pumping. He said there is no specific Hollis Road budget line, and a full rehab is planned as one large item.

budget_items.topic: Fine for further silt events at 615 Townsend Street
budget_items.what_was_said: A member proposed a daily fine on the landowner if silt again reaches Page Pond without remediation in place.
The state extended the existing trails grant, and a new recreational trails grant application was planned for a cart path at 260 Howard Street.
A member mentioned in passing that a home elevator can be installed for a certain cost.

decisions.decision: 41 Country Lane continued to December 1 so the applicant can reorient the house and tanks and consider tree replacement.
101 Pleasant Street continued to December 1. The applicant is to stake the driveway, house corners, septics and replication area, and a site walk is set for the Saturday after Thanksgiving.
The commission agreed to wait two weeks for Casey's review before deciding whether to require a wetland specialist at 615 Townsend Street.
Written notice to the landowner will state that further silt reaching Page Pond will draw a daily fine, and any further instructions to him will be in writing.
A site walk on Saturday, November 27 will cover 101 Pleasant Street, 260 Howard Street and 441 Townsend Harbor Road.

what_happened.line: The commission voted to send written notice that further silt reaching Page Pond from 615 Townsend Street will bring a daily fine until remediation is in place.
It tabled for two weeks the question of requiring a wetland specialist at 615 Townsend Street, pending legal review of the scope of work.
The 101 Pleasant Street subdivision and 41 Country Lane were each continued to December 1; 188 Whalen Road was also continued to December 1.
Negative determinations were voted for a Lancaster Ave garage, a Peninsula Drive screen porch (the addition was denied) and work at 37 Pearl.
The commission declined to use the town's right of first refusal on the Chapter 61A land on Holmen Street and will send the selectmen a letter saying so.

why_it_matters: The Townsend Street vote sets up a possible daily fine on a landowner and may bring legal costs to the town, which are paid from the town budget, mostly taxes.
Passing on the Holmen Street right of first refusal means the town did not move to buy that Chapter 61A land, a decision that rests with the selectmen's follow-up.
watch_next: The two-week return of the wetland-specialist question for 615 Townsend Street, after legal review of the scope of work.
The December 1 continued hearings for 41 Country Lane, 101 Pleasant Street and 188 Whalen Road, and the November 27 site walk.
